issues.description: Extract a named predicate for 'layer statement without block' instead of an inline negated conjunction.
issues.detail: The expression `!(nodeName === 'layer' && typeof node.nodes === 'undefined')` buries the actual rule inside a five-clause `&&` chain. A named helper like `isLayerStatement(node)` would surface the contract — layer statement form is allowed before `@import`, layer block form is not — at the call site.

issues.description: Replace `typeof node.nodes === 'undefined'` with a clearer null/shape check.
issues.detail: PostCSS models block-less at-rules by absence of `nodes` and block-having ones by an array. Prefer `node.nodes == null` (codebase-conventional, Pike) or an `'nodes' in node` shape check (Liskov) so the AST contract is named rather than probed via defensive `typeof` verbiage.

issues.description: Add a positive test for `@layer foo;` (statement form) before `@import` to lock the accept-case.
issues.detail: The new test only covers the reject case (`@layer foo {}` before `@import`). The complementary accept case — block-less `@layer foo;` before `@import` must remain valid — is the other half of the distinction. Without it, a future predicate refactor could silently regress the allowed form.

synthesis.summary: The panel unanimously agrees the fix is correct and minimal: it restores the CSS spec distinction between layer statements (block-less, allowed before `@import`) and layer rules (with block, not allowed). All three reviewers flag the same trio of expression-hygiene concerns, none structural. The predicate buries intent in a negated conjunction with a defensive `typeof` check, and tests cover the reject case but not the symmetric accept case. Recommended action: extract a named predicate, use a shape-appropriate null check, and add the statement-form accept test.
